item.title: Twine: Buy and Sell CKB Without Depositing on an Exchange (Fiber P2P PoC) (1 posts)
item.description: Update: sell-only book, and JIT inbound at release 1. The book is sell-only A post offers CKB. The poster is the seller. The taker is the buyer. There is no buy post. The last build had both sides: sell (offering CKB) and buy (bidding for CKB). A buy post made the taker the seller. take had no invoice. Both sides got need-invoice, and the buyer sent payout-invoice before any hold existed. That path is gone. new-order with side other than sell is refused. Taking a leftover buy post is refused. take always carries the buyer’s payout invoice. The hold is created there. No need-invoice round trip on take. The app no longer has Buy / Sell tabs. item.title: Noir-CKB update: what I decided after the direction check, what you can try today, and where this is going (1 posts)
item.description: Update: the setup ceremony for the private tally is open. The circuit is frozen at tag private-tally-v2-circuit-freeze and the first contribution is in (mine, as Xiaomao). The beacon will be the hash of CKB mainnet block 20,870,000, so contributions need to land before then, roughly by 30 October. Why it matters: the private tally won’t go to testnet with a single-party key. With a ceremony, the key is safe as long as one contributor throws away their randomness. How to contribute: You need a laptop with Node.js 18+. It’s a relay, one person at a time, because each key builds on the previous one. item.title: From CKB transactions to wallet connections: three design lessons from CCC (1 posts)
item.description: Sending 100 CKB sounds simple: choose a recipient, enter the amount, and sign. For a DApp developer, that means deciding which cells to spend, creating the recipient’s output and any change, calculating a fee, and getting the transaction signed through the user’s wallet. Those pieces depend on one another. Adding inputs changes the transaction’s size, and the size changes the fee. Different wallets can also require different signing steps. CKBers’ Codebase (CCC) is a TypeScript SDK that helps applications handle these details. Our work, When EVM Defaults Break: Three SDK Patterns for UTXO-Family Wallets, draws three design lessons from the work already done in CCC. It is a collaboration...
